subject: Private deployment: selecting attachment mode and next steps for NetOps
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@fincart.com>, Zoe Park <zoe.park@fincart.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 May 2028 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment: selecting attachment mode and next steps for NetOps

Hi Alex / Zoe — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and the concrete asks so your NetOps and procurement teams can evaluate: 

Summary of options we discussed:
- Hosted API (fastest) — requires minimal network changes, traffic to redwood-public endpoints; suitable for PII-free, low-risk workloads.
- Dedicated capacity — single-tenant GPU pool on our infra; data-in-transit stays over TLS to public endpoints but billing + compute isolation improves.
- Private deployment (VPC / on-prem) — full network isolation; two primary attachment patterns we recommend for AWS customers: PrivateLink endpoint per account vs VPC Peering (or Transit Gateway) for higher-throughput workloads.

NetOps asks we need answered to recommend the final path:
1) Can your NetOps create either PrivateLink endpoints (interface VPC endpoints) in the target account, or do they prefer a managed VPC Peering/Transit Gateway approach? If PrivateLink, we provide NLB endpoint service names.
2) Egress expectations: will traffic originate from your VPC to Redwood, or do you expect inbound flows to your VPC? We typically see egress-only (your requests to Redwood) but some customers run callbacks.
3) CIDR/IP policy: do you have a stable allowlist range we can consume, or should we provide static egress IPs for inbound firewall rules?
4) TLS and mTLS: do you require mutual TLS termination at the endpoint? We support mTLS for PrivateLink; for peering we recommend TLS from client to our service endpoint.
5) Timeline & procurement: ideal go-live window and any procurement milestones (PO, SOW signature).

I attached a simple network sketch and a starter SOW draft for your procurement team. Next steps I propose:
- Alex / Zoe: share NetOps contact + preferred attachment model by EOD Thu 5/24.
- Ben: I asked NetOps for IP/endpoint specs once Fincart chooses a mode.
- Marissa: drafting SOW updates for the chosen deployment.

If you want, we can run a short follow-up with our NetOps (Ben) and your network engineer to walk through the PrivateLink service name and security constraints.

Thanks — Jordan
-- 
Jordan Blake

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@fincart.com>

Date: Wed, 22 May 2028 08:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment: selecting attachment mode and next steps for NetOps

Hi Jordan — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifying questions from NetOps (I've copied Zoe + procurement).

1) Our preference is PrivateLink if performance is within acceptable latency bounds; otherwise we'll consider a Transit Gateway peering model. Can you share the expected RTT (p95) to an interface endpoint in us-west-2 when using your private deployment?
2) For PrivateLink, do you need our account ID or can we create an endpoint service on our side and share the ARN?
3) Egress IPs: we prefer allowing a small CIDR block over a long-lived list of individual IPs. Can Redwood provide a recommended CIDR or will we be expected to allow a set of fixed IPs?
4) We will need an internal runbook for DNS resolution and certificate provisioning. Can Redwood provide a step-by-step for DNS + TLS + health checks?

Timeline: procurement is targeting a PO by 6/15 if NetOps validates the connectivity pattern. Can you confirm if that aligns with your delivery timelines?

Thanks,
Alex
VP Platform Engineering
Alex Chen | alex.chen@fincart.com

[Attached: internal_netops_req_form.xlsx]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 22 May 2028 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment: selecting attachment mode and next steps for NetOps

Alex — great questions. Short answers up front, details below.

- Latency: for us-west-2 PrivateLink we typically see p95 token latency add of ~8-15ms compared to hosted public endpoints; we'll run a short probe from our side once you provision an endpoint.
- Endpoint provisioning: Fincart should create the Interface Endpoint in your account and then share the ENI/Service endpoint ID; alternatively we can create a service and share the ServiceName — both work.
- IP allowlist/CIDR: we can support either static egress IPs (we'll publish a small set of fixed IPs via a signed manifest) or you can allow a /27 from our transit pool for the customer. We're comfortable publishing a /28 for most customers; Ben will confirm specifics.
- DNS/TLS runbook: Ben, can you drop the DNS/TLS checklist and the PrivateLink health-check config? We'll include it in the final runbook for Fincart.

Timeline: PO by 6/15 is doable on our side for an initial pilot if NetOps validation completes by 6/1. We can commit to a provisioning slot in the week of 6/12 for the PrivateLink setup.

Proposed next step: 30-min NetOps sync (Ben + your network engineer) to finalize whether PrivateLink or Transit Gateway should be used. Please let me know a few time slots.

Regards,
Jordan

Alex / Jordan — adding a few technical specifics for your NetOps team to evaluate (pasting as a short checklist). I attached a compact network sketch with the NLB/service name.

PrivateLink checklist for NetOps:
- Create Interface Endpoint in us-west-2 (type: Interface) in the VPC where Redwood traffic originates.
- Security groups: allow outbound to NLB port 443; inbound rules only necessary if you run callbacks.
- DNS: enable private-dns for the endpoint if you want our service name to resolve to the ENI IPs; otherwise point an internal CNAME to the provided DNS name.
- TLS: Redwood provides server certs. If you require mTLS, upload your client cert bundle to our portal and we'll enable client-auth on the PrivateLink NLB.
- Health checks: HTTP/HTTPS 200 on /_health; we can customize path.
- Egress IPs: we can offer a published set of 6 IPs for your firewall rules or reserve a /28. For strict allowlist-only environments we recommend the /28 reservation.
- Monitoring: VPC Flow Logs + our endpoint metrics; we'll share Grafana links once live.

Performance note: PrivateLink is constrained by ENI bandwidth per interface — if you expect sustained high throughput (many concurrent streams) consider Transit Gateway peering; it's slightly more operational work but scales better.

Next steps from our side:
- Jordan: schedule 30-min NetOps sync (I'll join).
- Alex: share your NetOps contact and a preferred 3-slot availability window.
- Marissa: I'll send the finalized SOW snippet for PrivateLink + pricing for reserved capacity if they prefer a blended model.

Attached: fincart_network_sketch_v2.pdf

Thanks,
